pathway.title: ELDORADO GOLD CORP /FI — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Business quality is adequate and carried by four operating mines. Reported EBITDA margin on metal sales was 57.04% for nine months and EBITDA covered cash interest 11.72x at a realized gold price of US$4,326 per ounce, so the operating base services its debt comfortably while gold stays near today's level. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C3

- Leverage visibility is weak. Net debt rose by US$1,182.90 million in nine months to US$1,588.60 million at 2026-09-30, or US$1,608.22 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-12-15; no trailing-twelve-month EBITDA exists, so leverage is not calculated, and on nine months of EBITDA alone net debt is 1.82x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

- Free cash flow stability is weak until the new mines produce. Consolidated free cash flow was negative US$654.3 million for nine months, while the issuer's measure excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay was positive US$202.1 million, so the two projects explain the gap and their delivery decides when cash flow turns. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C8

- Liquidity is adequate near term but the maturity profile is back-loaded. Liquidity of US$671.53 million covers the US$283.60 million of principal due in two years 2.37x, but US$958.80 million falls due in the third year, including US$325.0 million drawn on the Credit Facility and US$500.0 million of Senior Notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C4; calculation C5

- Refinancing capacity is average. The Credit Facility was enlarged and extended to 2029-03-01 and the issuer's fair value for the Senior Notes was 98.38% of face value, but no rating, market quote or peer comparison is supplied, so access to capital markets is inferred from a single disclosure. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C7

- Execution risk is the primary downside path. Skouries capital rose 22.84% in two revisions, Kisladag cost per ounce rose sharply, and guidance was cut, so a further slip would meet the third-year maturities with the build unfinished. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_eldoradogoldreportsfirstqu.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C10

- Concentration and shareholder returns are the governance-related constraints. Lamaque produced 46.83% of third-quarter revenue, gold was 90.35% of contract revenue, and dividends and share cancellations took US$138.00 million in nine months while net debt rose. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 19; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C9

runs.text: The first strength is a cost-advantaged operating base that converts price into cash. Lamaque earns the largest share of revenue at the lowest cost per ounce, and the realized price exceeded all-in sustaining cost by US$2,276 per ounce, which supports interest cover of 11.72x and lets the operating mines absorb a large price fall before sustaining cost is uncovered. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C6; calculation C3

The second strength is near-term liquidity. Cash of US$396.83 million and US$274.7 million available on the Credit Facility give US$671.53 million against US$283.60 million of principal due in two years, so scheduled principal through 2028 does not depend on market access. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C4

The third strength is the funding of Foran in shares and the larger, longer Credit Facility, which avoided a debt-funded acquisition and moved the parent's secured maturity to 2029-03-01. The fourth is the diversification that the new mines add, which should lower the share of Lamaque and of gold in cash flow once they produce. The fifth is independent governance with effective internal control and stated covenant compliance. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is a rising and unfinished build. Net debt rose to US$1,588.60 million while the projects absorb capital, so deleveraging waits for commercial production in late fourth quarter 2026, and a slip lengthens the period over which debt grows. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C1

The second weakness is a back-loaded maturity profile with US$958.80 million due in the third year, the third is repeated cost and schedule slippage that weakens confidence in management estimates, the fourth is concentration in one mine and one metal, and the fifth is a legal structure that puts the Greek assets behind project lenders while the sources do not rank the instruments. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C5; calculation C11

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one acquisition in the period is Foran Mining Corporation, completed on 2026-04-14 and paid almost entirely in newly issued shares, with a nominal cash component and replacement options. It added the McIlvenna Bay copper, zinc, gold and silver project in Saskatchewan and brought in the Sprott Credit Facility, an equipment finance facility and government contribution obligations at fair value, so parent creditors gained a ramp-up asset and secured Canadian debt carrying a Company guarantee, and the share issue did not repay existing borrowing. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C9

There was no new bond issue in the period. New borrowing came from the Senior Secured Credit Facility, which was raised to US$450 million on 2026-05-26 and to US$600 million on 2026-08-12 with a later maturity and drawn to US$325.0 million, and from the final euro 60.0 million draw on the Contingent Overrun Facility, which brought the Skouries Term Facility to its full size. The Skouries equity commitment was completed in the third quarter, so the letter of credit that backstopped it is nil. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 8

Other transactions were smaller: an additional stake in Amex Exploration lifted the associate holding to about 27% in December 2025, the investment in Probe Metals was sold in the first quarter of 2026 for about US$42 million, and the Romania segment was disposed in the fourth quarter of 2025. No sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout or recapitalisation is disclosed. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.value: Net debt is where this credit has changed. Total debt at carrying value rose from US$1,275.05 million at 2025-12-31 to US$1,985.43 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash fell from US$869.36 million to US$396.83 million, so net debt rose from US$405.70 million to US$1,588.60 million. Three events drove it: the Foran acquisition on 2026-04-14 brought in the Sprott Credit Facility, an equipment facility and government contribution obligations; the Senior Secured Credit Facility was drawn to US$325.0 million; and capital spending on property, plant and equipment reached US$1,210.02 million in nine months against US$425.75 million of operating cash flow, with the third-quarter release attributing most of that quarter's spending to Skouries and McIlvenna Bay. The mechanism is a build phase funded by the balance sheet, so net debt keeps rising until both projects reach commercial production, which the company expects in late fourth quarter 2026; the consequence for creditors is a leverage path that depends on project delivery. A ratio against a full year of earnings is not calculated because the 2025 annual statements are not in the files supplied.

fields.value: Coverage is strong on the figures that exist. Nine-month reported EBITDA of US$873.69 million was 11.72x the US$74.55 million of cash interest paid, and the same ratio was 10.62x a year earlier, so cover did not deteriorate while debt rose. The cash interest figure includes US$45.94 million of capitalized interest paid in investing activities; counting only the interest expensed would have flattered the ratio. This ratio uses nine months and the report's own definitions, so it is not a test of the Credit Facility interest cover covenant, which is measured on rolling four quarters.

fields.value: Operations do not yet fund the build. Operating cash flow of continuing operations was US$425.75 million for nine months, held down by working capital that absorbed US$113.27 million, driven by a US$145.34 million build in inventories, and by income taxes paid of US$227.80 million against US$120.14 million a year earlier. Investing outflows of US$1,087.12 million were met by cash on hand and by financing inflows of US$199.36 million, while dividends of US$54.10 million and share cancellations of US$83.90 million also left in the period. Shareholder returns during a build phase compete with deleveraging, and the first test is whether fourth-quarter capital spending falls once commercial production starts.

fields.value: Liquidity covers scheduled principal for the next two years but not the third year on its own, and it is before further project capital spending. Cash of US$396.83 million and US$274.7 million available on the Credit Facility give US$671.53 million, down from US$975.96 million at 2025-12-31, against principal due of US$141.05 million within one year and US$142.55 million in year two. Year three then holds US$958.80 million, including the Credit Facility drawings of US$325.0 million due 2029-03-01 and the Senior Notes of US$500.0 million due 2029-09-01, so refinancing risk concentrates in a single window. Restricted cash of US$71.90 million is held for Term Facility repayments and is not counted, and interest is excluded from the ladder. The only facility with a stated expiry inside twelve months is the VAT Facility, a revolving line of EUR 30.0 million for reimbursable value added tax that matures by 2027-06-30.

fields.value: Third-quarter financing events changed the funding mix. The Credit Facility was drawn by US$225.0 million in the quarter, taking nine-month drawings to US$325.0 million, and on 2026-08-12 it was amended to raise availability from US$450 million to US$600 million, extend maturity to 2029-03-01 and improve pricing and covenant terms. The Skouries equity commitment was completed in the quarter, so the letter of credit that backstopped it, EUR 206.8 million at 2025-12-31, is nil. The Term Facility is now fully drawn at EUR 740.4 million after a EUR 60.0 million draw on the Contingent Overrun Facility during the nine months, and EUR 63.3 million sits in the Debt Service Reserve Account. The operating milestones are first copper-gold concentrate at Skouries and the ramp-up of McIlvenna Bay, both with commercial production expected in late fourth quarter 2026, while 2026 production guidance was cut in the quarter.

fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are small beside it, and covenant headroom is not established. Lease liabilities of US$14.203 million sit on their own lines outside Total Debt, with US$24.595 million of undiscounted lease payments in the commitments table; the employee benefit plan obligation of US$14.514 million, the asset retirement obligation of US$139.709 million plus a US$5.866 million current portion and derivative liabilities of US$8.509 million are also outside it. The commitments table lists only obligations that changed significantly, so purchase and capacity commitments are not established, and the statements and release disclose no litigation, consent-decree, factoring or supply-chain finance funding. On covenants, the Credit Facility requires interest cover of at least 3.00 to 1.00 and net leverage of no more than 3.50 to 1.00 on rolling four-quarter periods, the Term Facility has debt service and leverage covenants whose levels are not stated, and the Senior Notes restrict distributions and material asset sales; the issuer reports compliance with every covenant at 2026-09-30 but prints no covenant ratio.

fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is operating strength. EBITDA margin on metal sales was 57.04% for nine months against 41.10% a year earlier, and the issuer's free cash flow excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay was positive at US$202.1 million, so the operating mines generate cash after their own capital spending. That view would win if both projects reach commercial production on schedule and capital spending drops; it would lose if the ramp-up keeps slipping, as the cut in Skouries 2026 gold guidance to 10,000 to 35,000 ounces suggests, and the Credit Facility is drawn further to cover the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for ELDORADO GOLD CORP /FI as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the transaction, ownership, business, operating-model, governance and sponsor-behaviour facts in the seven supplied documents, to 2026-09-30, with events dated after the balance-sheet date kept apart from period facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used. Dates above are those printed in each document.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Eldorado is a listed producer with no controlling shareholder disclosed and conventional governance, so creditor risk comes from capital allocation: two new mines are consuming debt-funded capital while dividends and buybacks continue under a newly installed chief executive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 1; 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 1; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skouries project capital has risen from about US$1,160 million to US$1,425 million in two revisions, and nine-month dividends of US$54.10 million and buybacks of US$83.90 million were paid while both new mines were still absorbing cash. No distressed amendment, waiver or exchange is disclosed and the Skouries term debt is non-recourse to the parent, but no source ranks the instruments, so legal protection is not established. The sponsor and governance risk level is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_eldoradogoldreportsfirstqu.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership gives no sponsor to assess, which removes sponsor-extraction risk but leaves control unverified. The documents name no controlling shareholder, and the only holder class identified is the former Foran shareholders, who received 24.72% of the shares in issue in April 2026; a holder with a large stake would change this finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 1; 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation is the main governance risk. Dividends and share cancellations totalled US$138.00 million in nine months, 32.41% of operating cash flow of US$425.75 million, while the Credit Facility was drawn to US$325.0 million and the two new mines absorbed capital. Returns that compete with project completion delay deleveraging, and the new chief executive's stated aim to balance debt reduction, reinvestment and shareholder returns is management language with no disclosed limit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C8; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Project execution has repeatedly cost more than planned, which weakens the reliability of management estimates. The Skouries estimate rose 22.84% in two revisions, the McIlvenna Bay estimate rose by about US$23 million, and the midpoint of 2026 gold guidance was cut 71.88% for Skouries and 17.81% for the group, so the cash flow meant to repay the build debt arrives later than first planned.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_eldoradogoldreportsfirstqu.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_eldoradogoldreportsq22026f.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - One mine and one commodity carry the cash flow. Lamaque produced 46.83% of third-quarter revenue and gold was 90.35% of contract revenue, so a gold-price fall or a Lamaque disruption reaches cash flow before copper from the new mines can diversify it; the mix is moving slowly as by-product sales grow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 19; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The legal structure splits debt into three pools and no source ranks them. The Skouries term debt of US$818.42 million is non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries Project and the Hellas Gold operating assets, the parent carries US$816.53 million of Senior Notes with subsidiary guarantees and Credit Facility debt, and the Canadian debt of US$350.48 million, mostly the Sprott Credit Facility, is secured on the Foran assets with a Company guarantee. This implies that cash from the Greek assets reaches parent creditors only after project debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C10; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance structure is conventional and independent, but leadership changed within two months of commissioning. The board committees are independent and the auditor reports effective internal control for 2025, yet the chair, the lead independent director, a committee chair, the chief executive and the chief financial officer's remit all changed between 2026-07-30 and 2026-09-30; the former chief executive stays on the board, which preserves continuity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 8; 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 9; 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 10; 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 11; 40-F_2025-12-31_ego-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 12; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-30_eldoradogoldreportsq22026f.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Foran acquisition was equity-funded, which protects creditors from a debt-funded deal, but it brought assumed debt of US$355.32 million and a ramp-up risk. Shares were 99.61% of the consideration, and the mine added only US$9.6 million of third-quarter revenue and a US$3.5 million loss while ramping up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C9; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that the operating mines fund themselves: the issuer's free cash flow excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay was US$202.1 million for nine months, the Foran deal was paid in shares, the new chief executive has put capital discipline and balance-sheet strength first, and the issuer reports compliance with every covenant at 2026-09-30. Skouries produced its first concentrate on 2026-09-08 and was connected to grid power on 2026-09-28, so the main construction milestones are behind the project, although commissioning continues. Taken together these would support a Low risk level.

fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 7; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_eldoradogoldreportsq32026f.htm.jsonl, page 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve to Low if both mines reach commercial production in late fourth quarter 2026 without a further capital revision, buybacks pause while net debt is falling and dividends stay within operating cash flow. It would worsen to High if capital estimates rise again, if the Credit Facility is drawn further to fund distributions, if a large shareholder with an extraction record appears, or if executed agreements show wide capacity for restricted payments and priming.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No shareholder register, insider holding or control agreement is supplied, so the finding that there is no sponsor to assess could change if a large holder exists, and sponsor behaviour is not scored.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Committee membership and independence are stated as at the annual report, and the later departure of the chair and a committee chair means current committee composition is not established, which could strengthen or weaken the governance view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual information form, reserve and life-of-mine data, offtake terms and customer concentration are not supplied, so revenue durability beyond the next year and buyer concentration are not assessed and the diversification finding rests on production and revenue by mine.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capacity for distributions, debt and liens cannot be assessed because no executed agreement is supplied; the Senior Notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances, but without the baskets the risk level could rise if capacity proves wide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital cost and guidance figures are management estimates dated October 2026 and have changed with every release, so the cost-escalation finding holds only as at the third-quarter release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one acquisition in the period is Foran Mining Corporation, completed on 2026-04-14 and paid almost entirely in newly issued shares, with a nominal cash component and replacement options. It added the McIlvenna Bay copper, zinc, gold and silver project in Saskatchewan and brought in the Sprott Credit Facility, an equipment finance facility and government contribution obligations at fair value, so parent creditors gained a ramp-up asset and secured Canadian debt carrying a Company guarantee, and the share issue did not repay existing borrowing.

fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There was no new bond issue in the period. New borrowing came from the Senior Secured Credit Facility, which was raised to US$450 million on 2026-05-26 and to US$600 million on 2026-08-12 with a later maturity and drawn to US$325.0 million, and from the final euro 60.0 million draw on the Contingent Overrun Facility, which brought the Skouries Term Facility to its full size. The Skouries equity commitment was completed in the third quarter, so the letter of credit that backstopped it is nil.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions were smaller: an additional stake in Amex Exploration lifted the associate holding to about 27% in December 2025, the investment in Probe Metals was sold in the first quarter of 2026 for about US$42 million, and the Romania segment was disposed in the fourth quarter of 2025. No sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout or recapitalisation is disclosed.

fields.value: The strongest evidence for a stronger view is the cushion in the gold price. The realized price exceeded all-in sustaining cost by US$2,276 per ounce in the third quarter, so the price would have to fall 52.61% before the operating mines stopped covering sustaining cost, and the issuer's free cash flow excluding the two projects was positive US$202.1 million for nine months. Net debt is only 1.82x nine-month EBITDA, and the Foran acquisition was paid in shares. Together these argue that leverage on a full year will prove moderate once the build ends.

fields.value: The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that the cushion belongs to the operating mines while the debt belongs to the build. Project capital has risen twice, the 2026 gold guidance was cut, and the Credit Facility has absorbed the gap. The view would improve if both mines declare commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and capital spending falls, if the third-quarter measures of cost per ounce hold, and if trailing-twelve-month EBITDA, once available, shows leverage well inside the Credit Facility test. It would worsen if a further capital revision, a slower ramp-up or a gold price fall toward sustaining cost arrives before the 2029 maturities, or if distributions continue while the Credit Facility is drawn further.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Eldorado is a gold, copper and base metals producer that sells gold as doré and gold, silver, lead, zinc and copper in concentrate from mines in Turkiye, Canada and Greece. Four mines produce today: Kisladag and Efemcukuru in Turkiye, the Lamaque Complex in Canada and Olympias in Greece. Skouries in Greece and McIlvenna Bay in Saskatchewan, the latter acquired with Foran on 2026-04-14, are ramping up toward commercial production expected in late fourth quarter 2026. Revenue of US$1,531.744 million for nine months came 45.20% from Canada, 36.27% from Turkiye and 18.53% from Greece. The credit linkage is that cash flow is visible only as far as the gold price and the Lamaque mine allow, and debt service on the build depends on projects that have not yet produced steady cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Eldorado is a listed Canadian company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor named in the documents, so financial policy is set by the board and management rather than an owner. Debt sits in three pools: the Skouries term debt of US$818.42 million is non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries Project and the Hellas Gold operating assets, the parent holds the Senior Notes, guaranteed by four wholly-owned subsidiaries, and the Credit Facility, and the Foran debt is secured on the acquired assets with a Company guarantee. Dividends and buybacks of US$138.00 million in nine months, a new chief executive and a new chair mean financial policy is being reset during commissioning. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium, and this module adopts that view without adding evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is price-driven and cyclical. Third-quarter revenue rose 17.74% to US$511.860 million although gold produced fell 7.67%, because the realized gold price rose 22.65% to US$4,326 per ounce, and royalties rose with price to US$31.8 million in the quarter. Gold is 90.35% of contract revenue and the Lamaque mine 46.83% of quarterly revenue, so revenue is concentrated and Eldorado is a price taker with no pass-through. Concentrate is sold under offtake agreements, and the release says copper-gold concentrate markets are highly competitive, so treatment terms are a second price risk once Skouries produces. The effect on credit is that interest cover is strong at today's price but offers no visibility beyond the next price move.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly fixed at mine level and rise with volume handled and with royalties. Production costs rose to US$199.8 million in the third quarter from US$164.1 million, total cash costs rose to US$1,415 per ounce sold and all-in sustaining cost to US$2,050, yet the margin over sustaining cost still rose to US$2,276 per ounce. Kisladag is the weak point: lower grade and slower mining lifted its total cash cost 77.85% and its sustaining cost 83.30%, and higher-grade ore stacked on the heap leach pad will show in production only toward the end of the fourth quarter and into 2027 because of a leach cycle of about 300 days. Margins can therefore be defended against moderate volume pressure but not against a combination of falling price and rising unit cost at Kisladag.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA does not yet convert to free cash flow. Operating cash flow of continuing operations was US$425.747 million for nine months against US$1,210.017 million of additions to property, plant and equipment, and income taxes paid rose to US$227.796 million from US$120.136 million. Interest is being capitalized: US$57.668 million of the US$95.328 million of nine-month finance costs went into project cost, so when Skouries starts commercial production reported finance costs will rise toward the cash interest already paid even though cash interest does not change. Capital spending is committed at the projects but discretionary at the operating mines: guidance for growth capital excluding the projects is US$395 million to US$430 million and for sustaining capital US$170 million to US$190 million, and the projects' remaining capital falls away as they finish. Cash conversion therefore depends on the build ending, not on the operating base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is price-based and gives no pricing power; position depends on cost, where Lamaque at US$1,436 per ounce of sustaining cost sits well below Kisladag at US$2,832. New entrants face high capital and permitting barriers, which Skouries shows: a project with a 2022 feasibility study reached first concentrate in September 2026 at a capital cost that rose in two revisions, so supply is slow to respond and incumbents hold their assets. There is no substitute for gold as a store of value, though copper and zinc by-products face industrial demand cycles. Buyer power is limited for doré but real for concentrate, because the company relies on a limited number of smelters and offtakers and Skouries volumes are contracted only for the next two years. Supplier power showed in the project overruns, where contractor workforce levels, temporary power generation and other execution costs raised capital, and in royalty burdens that rise with price. The credit consequence is that value accrues to cost position and execution, not to market structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These factors are material for a producer in three jurisdictions with euro and Canadian dollar costs. The Turkish corporate tax rate change produced a US$47.4 million deferred tax gain in nine months, foreign exchange translation of deferred tax balances produced a US$41.5 million loss, and royalties rose to US$115.7 million from US$79.6 million with price. Euro and Canadian dollar zero-cost collars cover US$6.9 million and US$8.0 million a month, the Term Facility has swaps fixing 70% of the variable euro rate at 3.11% and 2.748% to 2032-12-31, and forward contracts deliver euros every six months to meet Term Facility repayments. Sector prices and jurisdiction taxes therefore move debt service capacity directly, while currency effects are partly hedged and mainly affect the euro project debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: a high gold price over sustaining cost, a low-cost anchor mine at Lamaque, liquidity that covers two years of principal, an equity-funded acquisition and independent governance. Weaknesses: unfinished projects absorbing cash, rising net debt without a full-year earnings figure, a third-year maturity concentration, repeated capital revisions and concentration in one mine and one metal. Opportunities that could improve credit: commercial production at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, the Olympias expansion and Kisladag's higher-grade ore stacked in 2026 and 2027, and a pause in buybacks. Threats that could weaken credit: a fall in the gold price toward sustaining cost, a further overrun, Credit Facility drawings used for distributions and a failed refinancing of the 2029 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: nine-month revenue of US$1,531.744 million from four mines is mid-sized and the competitive advantage is cost at Lamaque rather than a moat. Business diversification is average because three jurisdictions are offset by 90.35% gold and a single mine at 46.83% of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because growth capital at the operating mines is discretionary while project capital is committed. Margin stability is average: the margin on metal sales was 57.04% but depends on price. Free cash flow stability is weak, with consolidated free cash flow negative US$654.3 million for nine months. Refinancing access is average, supported by the extended Credit Facility and a Senior Notes fair value of 98.38% of face value. Liquidity is adequate at US$671.53 million. Financial policy and governance are average, with distributions continuing during the build. The trend is a growing balance sheet whose debt was added ahead of the cash flow it is meant to repay, and the key missing data are trailing earnings and the debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The next 12 to 24 months are set by commissioning. Tailwinds are first concentrate at both new mines, grid power at Skouries from 2026-09-28, the Term Facility being fully drawn so no further project debt is available, Kisladag's higher-grade ore and the realized gold price. Headwinds are the start of Term Facility repayments on 2026-12-31, with US$141.05 million of principal due within one year, higher guided capital at the operating mines, revised and lower 2026 production guidance, and capitalized interest ending as projects start, which raises reported finance costs. Over three to five years Skouries has a stated mine life of 20 years and McIlvenna Bay of 18 years on management studies, which would diversify revenue toward copper, but those are management statements and the 2029 maturities arrive within that window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario that fits this issuer is a commissioning slip combined with a lower gold price. If Skouries or McIlvenna Bay fails to reach commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2026, project and accelerated operational capital continue beyond the estimate, free cash flow stays negative and cash falls from US$396.83 million while the Credit Facility is drawn from its US$274.7 million balance. Term Facility repayments begin on 2026-12-31 and dividends continue, so liquidity of US$671.53 million falls without the new mines' cash to replace it. A gold price fall would cut revenue directly because there is no pass-through, although the price would have to fall 52.61% to reach third-quarter sustaining cost. Management can pause buybacks and dividends, defer growth capital at the operating mines, draw the Credit Facility and sell investments. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months because liquidity covers principal due 2.37x, but not to meet the 2029 maturities from liquidity alone, so refinancing capacity would decide the outcome. The observable triggers are a missed commercial production date, a further capital revision and further Credit Facility drawings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Eldorado presents an adequate business profile supported by four producing mines, a gold price well above sustaining cost, covered cash interest and two years of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by net debt of US$1,588.60 million that rose while two projects absorbed capital, a back-loaded maturity profile and a legal structure whose ranking is not established. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at the operating mines and weak at consolidated level until the projects produce. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on commercial production, the gold price and the Credit Facility's 2029 maturity. The primary downside path is a commissioning slip that meets the 2029 maturities with the build unfinished. Further analysis would require trailing-twelve-month earnings, the debt documents and a rating or market quote. Top risk: execution at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay.
